## game toolset

Launching, stopping and inspecting the game, and opening, leaving and joining worlds and servers.

### game_launch

**Launch Minecraft** · sets state (repeating it changes nothing more)

Use this first in a session, to start Minecraft or attach to the running game.

It starts Minecraft if needed, waits for the main menu, and injects and connects the developer agent. A running game is only attached.

- A start first turns WebSockets on and encrypted WebSockets off in options.txt.
- Linux starts the game with the BEDROCK_MCP_LAUNCH_COMMAND shell command, else mcbe-gdk-linux; Windows uses the shell.
- Linux finds a game from any launcher by its process; it fails, listing them, when several run and pid picks none.
- size applies on Hyprland (and makes the window floating) and on Windows; elsewhere notes say it was left alone.
- A running game ignores args and env. Windows takes no env and at most one minecraft:// link.

Returns {pid, already_running, agent, window, menu_text, websocket_port, notes}. menu_text is the menu text OCR read.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `args` | array of string | Game arguments, e.g. one minecraft:// link |
| `env` | object | Extra environment for the launcher (Linux only) |
| `pid` | integer, at least 1 | The game process to attach to when several run |
| `size` | array of integer, at least 1 | [width, height] in logical pixels |
| `timeout_ms` | integer, at least 0 | Main-menu wait (default 300000) |

### world_open

**Open a world** · acts (repeating it acts again), may reach other machines

Use this to enter a local world before testing in it.

It clicks through the menus like a player: Play, the Worlds tab, then the card labelled exactly name, paging through the list. It waits until the player is in the world and gameplay shows. Call automation_connect next.

- An unknown name fails at once and lists the worlds; a name several worlds share fails and lists their folder ids and last-played times.
- For a folder id whose name others share, it picks that world's card by last-played order (needs the UI tree), and leaves and fails if another world loaded.
- It opens only local worlds: if the loading screen names another job or the world's files stay unwritten, it backs out and fails.
- The unstable screens capability tells the menus apart; without it, it looks for the name before clicking Play.
- It knows the player is in from the screens capability or the WebSocket, else from OCR seeing no menu or loading text (noted).
- It then waits up to 20 s for the HUD, or a pause or chat screen.
- A world already loading is waited for without clicks.
- Fails when already in a world (call world_leave first).

Returns {world: {name, folder}, clicked, waited, notes, next}. waited is wait_until's reply plus hud_ms.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (required) | string | The world's folder id, or the name the world list shows when no other world shares it (see worlds_list) |
| `timeout_ms` | integer, at least 0 | Wait for the player to be in the world (default 120000) |

### world_leave

**Leave the world** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this to return to the menus, for example before world_packs_set changes the world's packs.

It opens the pause menu with Escape when gameplay has the input, clicks Save & Quit, and waits up to 60 s for the main menu or the world list. The WebSocket stays connected; commands answer "Unknown command" until a world is open again.

- Without the unstable layer's screens capability it looks for Save & Quit before pressing Escape, and confirms the menu by OCR.
- Fails when the game is not in a world, or is still in it after Save & Quit.

Returns {clicked, waited_ms, notes}.

No arguments.

### server_join

**Join a server** · destructive, may reach other machines

Use this to test on a server instead of a local world.

It starts the game with minecraft://connect/?serverUrl=H&serverPort=P (the connect link on Microsoft Learn's Deep Link Handlers page), stopping a running game first, as game_launch does. Call wait_until in_world to know when the join finished.

- Refuses a non-loopback address unless allow_remote is set, since a remote join uses the signed-in account.
- local_server starts before the game and must bind its UDP port within 60 s; it fails when the port is already in use or the server exits.

Returns {address, link, restarted, note, local_server, launch}. local_server is {pid, port, log}; launch is game_launch's reply.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `address` (required) | string | host:port |
| `allow_remote` | boolean | Allow a non-loopback address; the join uses the signed-in account (default false) |
| `local_server` | object {command, port} | A server to start first; game_stop or the next local_server stops it, and its output goes to local-server.log in the agent directory |
| `timeout_ms` | integer, at least 0 | Main-menu wait after the restart (default 300000) |

### game_status

**Game status** · reads only

Use this to see the whole state at once before a test, or when a tool fails for an unclear reason.

It reads the game, agent, window, WebSocket, world and unstable layer in one call. Read attention and warnings first.

- attention is null while play can go on, else {kind, detail, next, source}: death (the live death screen, or Bridge pack health 0 when the unstable layer cannot tell) or disconnected. Check it when actions stop confirming.
- warnings are {kind, detail}; empty means a normal session. Kinds: death, disconnected, unstable_anchors_only (seen on Linux only), unstable_disabled, unstable_failed, unstable_capabilities, websocket_disconnected, screen_open, other_mods.
- in_world comes from the screens capability, else the WebSocket; null, with notes, when neither tells.
- world needs the WebSocket: with the Bridge pack, re_mcp:state (the player), re_mcp:world and nearby re_mcp:entities; without it, eye, yaw, pitch (bisected), dimension, nearby actors, time_of_day and game_time. Without the pack, in a world with the unstable layer's world_state capability, world.player adds the native player_get fields (source native), even without the WebSocket.
- On generic Linux desktops the window size is at scale 1 and workspace is null.

Returns {running, pid, crash_debugger, agent, window, in_world: {value, source, notes}, content_log_errors, attention, warnings, websocket, world, camera, recording, timeline, held, unstable}. window.desktop is hyprland, generic or windows; unstable is null without the layer, else {capabilities, screens (scene stacks, bottom first), camera}.

No arguments.

### hud_get

**Read the HUD text** · reads only

Use this to read the toasts, titles, action bar or chat your add-on shows.

It reads the HUD through the unstable layer's hud_text capability, without the Bridge pack or OCR, and fails when that is not active.

- toasts holds every toast since the DLL loaded, oldest first, at most 32.
- title, subtitle, actionbar, popup (item name) and tip are {text, changed_ms} or null. changed_ms is when the DLL first saw the text (Unix ms), null if it was there before.
- actionbar may still hold text after it faded from the screen: compare changed_ms with title_ticks (50 ms ticks). title and subtitle may read null even while the screen shows them.
- death comes from the camera's damage parameters or a JSON UI death screen (not Ore UI); shown is null when nothing tells.

Returns {toasts, title, subtitle, actionbar, title_ticks, popup, tip, chat, detail, fresh, death, notes}. Toasts are {seq, at_ms, kind (achievement, recipe_unlocked, message, ...), title, message, message_id, persistent}. chat lines are {kind (chat, system, ...), username, message, full (as drawn), duration (seconds left), seen}, oldest first. detail says why texts could not be read; fresh is whether they come from the answering frame. death is {shown, message, ticks, screen, texts, respawn_available}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chat_limit` | integer, 0 to 100 | Newest chat lines to return (default 20) |

### game_stop

**Stop Minecraft** · destructive

Use this to end a session or before a clean restart.

It releases held input, stops the camera path, finishes any recording and stops the local server, then stops Minecraft.

- Linux runs mcbe-gdk-linux stop for a game it launched, else sends the game SIGTERM.
- Windows closes the game window and terminates the game if it still runs 15 s later.

Returns {input_released, camera, recording, local_server, game}. game is {stopping, output}, {stopping: false, note} when Minecraft was not running, or {error}.

No arguments.

### game_crash

**Crash Minecraft** · destructive

Use this only to test crash handling.

It makes the agent crash Minecraft on purpose, the way kind names. Wine's or Windows' crash handling takes over, and the game is gone afterwards.

Returns {crashed, note}. The agent replies before it crashes the game; game_status crash_debugger shows whether the crash handler runs.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` (required) | `"panic"` \\| `"access_violation"` \\| `"stack_overflow"` \\| `"abort"` | How the agent crashes the game |

## player toolset

The player: state, inventory, looking and the hotbar.

### player_get

**Read a player** · reads only

Use this to check a player's position, health, effects or other state after an action.

Reads a player's state from the bedrock-mcp Bridge pack, else from the game's local server through the unstable layer, else with vanilla commands.

- The Bridge pack (source "bridge") fills every field. It is asked only while Minecraft's WebSocket is connected.
- Without it, in single player with the unstable layer's world_state capability (source "native", no cheats needed): name, id, dimension, location, yaw, pitch, health, hunger, saturation, selectedSlot and effects. While the WebSocket is connected, querytarget, testfor and tag list (cheats) add eye, gameMode and tags.
- Otherwise (source "command", needs cheats), querytarget, testfor and tag list give only id, dimension, eye, yaw, pitch (in 0.25 degree steps), gameMode and tags.
- Native reads find the player by name, or take the only player; with several players and no name they fall back to commands. Notes say which fields are missing and why.

Returns {name, id, dimension, location (feet), eye, velocity, yaw, pitch, health: {current, max}, hunger, saturation (native only), gameMode, selectedSlot, effects: [{id, amplifier, ticks}], tags, flags: {sneaking, sprinting, onGround, flying, gliding, swimming, inWater, sleeping, falling, climbing}, spawnPoint, level, source, notes}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | "self" (default) for the player who ran /connect, or the name of another player such as a GameTest simulated player |

### player_set

**Set a player's state** · sets state (repeating it changes nothing more)

Use this to move a player or set its game mode, health or velocity for a test.

Writes the given fields once, then reads the player back.

- With the Bridge pack the Script API writes on the next tick: a teleport for location, rotation and dimension, setGameMode, the health component's setCurrentValue, and clearVelocity plus applyImpulse for velocity.
- A write the game refuses goes into rejected and notes with its reason; the rest still apply. applyImpulse can throw (Microsoft Learn's Entity reference), so velocity may land in rejected.
- Without the pack (needs cheats), /tp (with execute in for the dimension) and /gamemode set location, rotation, dimension and game mode; health and velocity fail.
- Fails when no field is given.

Returns {applied, rejected: {field: reason}, player (the player_get result)}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | "self" (default) for the player who ran /connect, or the name of another player such as a GameTest simulated player |
| `dimension` | `"overworld"` \\| `"nether"` \\| `"the_end"` | Teleport into this dimension (at location, or the same coordinates) |
| `game_mode` | `"survival"` \\| `"creative"` \\| `"adventure"` \\| `"spectator"` | Game mode to set |
| `health` | number, at least 0 | Current health to set; needs the Bridge pack |
| `location` | object {x, y, z} | Feet position to teleport to |
| `rotation` | object {pitch, yaw} | Bedrock degrees; a missing angle keeps its current value |
| `velocity` | object {x, y, z} | Velocity in blocks per tick; needs the Bridge pack |

### inventory_get

**Read a player's inventory** · reads only

Use this to check which items a player holds after a give, pickup or craft.

Reads a player's inventory and equipment.

- Empty slots are left out.
- Needs the bedrock-mcp Bridge pack; without it the call fails with the install steps.

Returns {size, selectedSlot, slots: [{slot, id, amount, maxAmount, stackable, name, lore, tags, canDestroy, canPlaceOn, keepOnDeath, lockMode, components, durability, enchantable, food, cooldown, potion}], equipment: {Head, Chest, Legs, Feet, Mainhand, Offhand}}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | "self" (default) for the player who ran /connect, or the name of another player such as a GameTest simulated player |

### hotbar_select

**Select a hotbar slot** · sets state (repeating it changes nothing more)

Use this to hold a different hotbar item; inside a fight, use a hotbar_select step in action_sequence instead.

Sets the player's selectedSlotIndex through the Bridge pack and reads the slot back.

- Without the pack, actor self presses the slot key (key.hotbar.N, as input_send {"hotbar": slot + 1} does) and confirms it with the native selectedSlot read (unstable world_state capability, single player; source native). A note says when the read is unavailable or shows another slot.
- Simulated players need the Bridge pack's GameTest; without it the call fails.

Returns {selectedSlot}, the slot read back (null when no read answered).

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `slot` (required) | integer, 0 to 8 | Hotbar slot to select, 0 (leftmost) to 8 |
| `actor` | string | "self" (default) for the player who ran /connect, or the name of another player such as a GameTest simulated player |

### look_at

**Turn a player** · sets state (repeating it changes nothing more)

Use this to aim a player before an action that needs a direction.

Turns a player, measured from its eye, to a yaw and pitch, toward a position, or toward an entity's eyes. frames spreads the turn over that many game ticks (50 ms each) along the shortest way.

- Give exactly one of yaw and pitch, position or entity_id.
- Each step is re_mcp:look with the Bridge pack (a teleport in place, no chat output, no cheats), else /tp (needs cheats).
- Without the pack an entity is aimed at its querytarget position, which is at eye height only for players.
- A simulated player gets a GameTest look instead, since a teleport's pitch does not last on it. It holds until its next look, turns at its own pace and ignores frames.

Returns {requested: {yaw, pitch}, confirmed (simulated players only: the rotation read back matches), player (the player_get result read afterwards)}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | "self" (default) for the player who ran /connect, or the name of another player such as a GameTest simulated player |
| `entity_id` | string | Look at this entity's eyes (its id from entities_list) |
| `frames` | integer, at least 0 | Steps, one per tick; 0 or 1 snaps |
| `pitch` | number, -90 to 90 | Positive looks down; give with yaw |
| `position` | object {x, y, z} | Look at this point |
| `yaw` | number | Bedrock degrees: 0 faces +Z (south), 90 faces -X (west); give with pitch |

## world toolset

Entities, blocks, containers, items, raycasts and world facts.

### target_get

**Read the crosshair target** · reads only

Use this to check what a player aims at before an attack or use.

Reads the block and the entity under the player's crosshair, up to 64 blocks away, with getBlockFromViewDirection and getEntitiesFromViewDirection.

- Needs the bedrock-mcp Bridge pack; without it the call fails with the install steps.

Returns {maxDistance, block: {id, location, states, ..., face, faceLocation, distance} or null, entity: {id, type, name, location, distance, health, tags} or null, miss}; miss is true when neither is hit.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | "self" (default) for the player who ran /connect, or the name of another player such as a GameTest simulated player |

### entities_list

**List nearby entities** · reads only

Use this to find entities near a player and their ids.

Lists entities within radius blocks of the player, nearest first, without the player. The first call fixes the list; pass next_cursor back as cursor until it is null to read each listed entity once.

- Sources, in order: the Bridge pack ("bridge"), the unstable layer's world_state capability ("native", single player only, see unstable_status), then querytarget and testfor ("command", needs cheats).
- bridge entries carry health and tags, and an entity that despawned since the first call shows as {id, removed: true}.
- native entries carry health. command entries carry id, location (eye height for players) and name, and type only when filtered by type.
- native and command pages come from the first call's list, so they miss later moves.
- bridge and native lists keep the nearest 4096 entities. An expired cursor fails; list again.

Returns {total, offset, entities: [{id, type, name, location, distance, ...}], next_cursor, source}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | "self" (default) for the player who ran /connect, or the name of another player such as a GameTest simulated player |
| `cursor` | string | next_cursor from the previous page; radius and type are ignored with it |
| `limit` | integer, 1 to 256 | Entities per page (default 16) |
| `radius` | number, at least 0 | Search radius in blocks around the player (default 32) |
| `type` | string | Only this entity type, e.g. minecraft:cow |

### entity_inspect

**Inspect an entity** · reads only

Use this to check an entity's position, health, tags or flags.

Reads one entity's identity and state by id.

- The Bridge pack (source "bridge") fills every field.
- Without it, the unstable layer's world_state capability (source "native", single player only, see unstable_status) reads id, type, name, nameTag, player, dimension, location, yaw, pitch and health; tags come from tag list when the WebSocket is connected (needs cheats).
- With neither, vanilla commands answer (source "command", needs cheats): querytarget, testfor and tag list give id, name, player, dimension, location (eye for players), yaw and tags.
- Commands cannot name an entity by id, so they select it by a spot around where querytarget saw it (a player by name), up to 2 blocks wide but under half the way to the nearest other entity. Each read is checked to have selected it, and an entity that moved is located again up to 5 times. They fail when another entity stands too close or it is in another dimension than the player.

Returns {id, type, name, nameTag, player, dimension, location, eye, velocity, yaw, pitch, viewDirection, health, tags, families, flags: {onGround, inWater, swimming, falling, climbing, sleeping, sneaking, sprinting}, source}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` (required) | string | An entity id from entities_list (Entity.id) |

### entity_components_get

**Read an entity's components** · reads only

Use this to check the component values your add-on gives an entity.

Reads an entity's Script API components. Each component's fields hold every readable property that is a number, string, boolean, vector or a list of them; objects with an id show as the id.

- Needs the bedrock-mcp Bridge pack; without it the call fails with the install steps.

Returns {id, type, components: [{type, fields}]}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` (required) | string | An entity id from entities_list (Entity.id) |

### entity_properties_get

**Read an entity's properties** · reads only

Use this to check the entity properties your add-on defines in an entity's behavior file; for dynamic properties set by scripts, use dynamic_properties_get.

Reads the named entity properties (defined in the entity's behavior file, e.g. minecraft:has_nectar) with getProperty.

- The stable Script API cannot list a type's properties, so name the ones to read.
- Entity properties are not private to a pack, so this reads the add-on's; dynamic properties are, which is why dynamic_properties_get reads them from the game instead.
- Without the Bridge pack, testfor has_property probes answer (source "command", needs cheats; entity selected as in entity_inspect, by type too when the unstable layer reads it): booleans by testing true and false, ints and floats by bisection between -2147483648 and 2147483647 (floats to 0.001), enums only among enum_values. At most 8 names; unread says why a name was not read.
- A refused command (no cheats) or a reply in another language than English fails the call with the reason.

Returns {id, type (from commands: the unstable layer's type, else null), properties: {name: value}, undefinedProperties (bridge: names the type does not define), unread (command: {name: reason}), source}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` (required) | string | An entity id from entities_list (Entity.id) |
| `enum_values` | object | Without the Bridge pack: candidate values per enum property name, e.g. {"wiki:color": ["red", "blue"]}; these names are read too |
| `names` | array of string | Entity property names to read |

### block_inspect

**Inspect a block** · reads only

Use this to check a block's id, states and contents after an action.

Reads the block at a location.

- The stable Script API has no solid flag, so none is returned.
- Needs the bedrock-mcp Bridge pack; without it the call fails with the install steps.

Returns {id, location, dimension, states (permutation states), tags, air, liquid, waterlogged, redstonePower (null when the block carries none), light, skyLight, components, inventory (slot count, or null)}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `location` (required) | object {x, y, z} | Block coordinates |
| `dimension` | `"overworld"` \\| `"nether"` \\| `"the_end"` | Default: the dimension of the player who ran /connect |

### raycast

**Cast a ray** · reads only

Use this to check what lies along a line, such as whether a path is clear.

Casts a ray with Dimension.getBlockFromRay and getEntitiesFromRay from a point along a direction vector, or along a Bedrock yaw and pitch.

- The player the ray starts from is left out of entities.
- A zero direction fails.
- Needs the bedrock-mcp Bridge pack; without it the call fails with the install steps.

Returns {from, direction, maxDistance, block: {..., face, faceLocation, distance} or null, entities: [{id, type, name, location, distance, ...}]}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | "self" (default) for the player who ran /connect, or the name of another player such as a GameTest simulated player |
| `direction` | object {x, y, z} | Direction vector; or give yaw and pitch |
| `from` | object {x, y, z} | Start point; default the actor's eye |
| `include` | array of `"blocks"` \\| `"entities"` | What the ray may hit (default both) |
| `max_distance` | number, at least 0 | Ray length in blocks (default 64) |
| `pitch` | number, -90 to 90 | Degrees, positive looks down; give with yaw instead of direction |
| `yaw` | number | Bedrock degrees: 0 faces +Z (south), 90 faces -X (west); give with pitch instead of direction |

### container_get

**Read a container** · reads only

Use this to check what a chest or other container holds.

Reads a block's or an entity's inventory without opening its screen, one page of slots at a time.

- Give location or entity_id, not both.
- Empty slots are left out; pass next back as offset until it is null.
- Needs the bedrock-mcp Bridge pack; without it the call fails with the install steps.

Returns {size, emptySlots, offset, slots: [{slot, id, amount, ...item details as in item_inspect}], next}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dimension` | `"overworld"` \\| `"nether"` \\| `"the_end"` | Default: the dimension of the player who ran /connect |
| `entity_id` | string | An entity id from entities_list (Entity.id) |
| `limit` | integer, at least 1 | Slots per page (default 27) |
| `location` | object {x, y, z} | A container block such as a chest |
| `offset` | integer, at least 0 | First slot (default 0) |

### item_inspect

**Inspect an item** · reads only

Use this to check one item stack's components, durability or lore in detail.

Reads one slot of the player's inventory, one of its equipment slots, or one slot of a container block or entity.

- Give slot or equipment, and at most one of location and entity_id. equipment reads the actor's own, so it takes neither.
- Needs the bedrock-mcp Bridge pack; without it the call fails with the install steps.

Returns {slot or equipment, item: {id, amount, maxAmount, stackable, name, lore, tags, canDestroy, canPlaceOn, keepOnDeath, lockMode, components, durability: {damage, max, unbreakable}, enchantable: {slots, enchantments}, food: {nutrition, saturationModifier, canAlwaysEat, usingConvertsTo}, cooldown: {category, ticks, remaining}, potion: {effect, durationTicks, delivery}}, or null for an empty slot}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | "self" (default) for the player who ran /connect, or the name of another player such as a GameTest simulated player |
| `dimension` | `"overworld"` \\| `"nether"` \\| `"the_end"` | Default: the dimension of the player who ran /connect |
| `entity_id` | string | Read the slot of this entity's inventory |
| `equipment` | `"Head"` \\| `"Chest"` \\| `"Legs"` \\| `"Feet"` \\| `"Mainhand"` \\| `"Offhand"` | An equipment slot of the actor instead of slot |
| `location` | object {x, y, z} | Read the slot of this container block |
| `slot` | integer, at least 0 | Inventory or container slot |

### world_info

**Read world info** · reads only

Use this to check the time, weather, difficulty and game rules.

Reads the world's state.

- The bedrock-mcp Bridge pack (source "bridge") fills every field.
- Without it, time query, weather query and gamerule answer (source "command", needs cheats) with timeOfDay, absoluteTime, day, weather, dimension and gameRules; moonPhase, difficulty and defaultSpawn are left out.
- From commands, gameRules keys are spelled as gamerule prints them, not as the Script API's camelCase names.
- A refused command (no cheats) or a reply in another language than English fails the call with the reason.

Returns {timeOfDay, absoluteTime, day, moonPhase, weather, difficulty, defaultSpawn, dimension (of the player who ran /connect), gameRules, source}.

No arguments.

### scoreboard_get

**Read scoreboards** · reads only

Use this to check the scores your add-on keeps.

Reads scoreboard objectives and their scores: every objective, or the one named.

- A named objective that does not exist gives an empty list.
- The bedrock-mcp Bridge pack answers when present (source "bridge").
- Without it, scoreboard objectives list and scoreboard players list * answer (source "command", needs cheats). participant is the name the game prints and type is null.
- A refused command (no cheats) or a reply in another language than English fails the call with the reason.

Returns {objectives: [{id, displayName, criteria (command only), scores: [{participant, type, score}]}], source}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `objective` | string | Objective id to read; default all objectives |

### dynamic_properties_get

**Read dynamic properties** · reads only

Use this to check the dynamic properties your add-on stored.

Reads every pack's dynamic properties on the world, a player or an entity from the game's own local server. A pack's Script API reads only its own; this needs no Bridge pack, cheats or Beta APIs.

- Needs the unstable layer's world_state capability (see unstable_status), so single player only; otherwise it fails and says why.
- truncated is true when a size bound cut the read or a number was not finite.

Returns {entity, collections: {<name as the game stores it>: {byteCount, properties: {<key>: {type: double|float|boolean|string|vector, value}}}}, truncated, tick (game tick of the read), readMicros}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target` (required) | string | "world", "player", or an entity id from entities_list |
| `pack` | string | Only this collection |
| `player` | string | With target "player": the player's name (default the first player) |

## actions toolset

Player input, menu clicks and gameplay actions.

### input_send

**Send input** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this to send raw keys, mouse moves and menu clicks that no gameplay tool covers.

Sends synthetic keyboard and mouse input through the agent injected into Minecraft (key messages and GameInput mouse readings), so bindings, menus and add-ons see real input. The window may be hidden or covered, and the real cursor stays free. To click a button by its label, ui_click is shorter.

- Order: release_all, pointer/cursor, release, move/jump/sneak/sprint, hold, hotbar, press, look, mouse, wheel/scroll, text, hold_ms, release_control.
- When the request also presses or holds a mouse button, the pointer hovers 500 ms first, since some screens (pause menu, world list) ignore a click before they saw the hover.
- look uses the Bridge pack's re_mcp:look when active (exact, no cheats, no chat feedback, one per frame), else /tp over the WebSocket, which needs cheats.
- Held controls stay down until released or the MCP session ends.
- Keep the window from being minimized.

Returns {held}: the controls still held down.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | array of number or null | Same as pointer, as [x, y]. |
| `hold` | array of string | Bindings from options.txt (key.jump, key.use, key.hotbar.1, key.chat), W3C key codes (KeyW, Digit1, Space, ShiftLeft, Escape, F5) or MouseLeft/MouseRight/MouseMiddle/MouseBack/MouseForward |
| `hold_ms` | integer, at least 0 | Release this request's hold controls after this long |
| `hotbar` | integer, 1 to 9 | Press key.hotbar.N |
| `jump` | boolean | Hold (true) or release (false) key.jump |
| `look` | object {frames, pitch, relative, yaw} | Turn the player to Bedrock yaw/pitch degrees (relative: by them) |
| `mouse` | object {x, y} | Raw relative mouse motion in counts (works without cheats); positive x turns right, positive y looks down; about 400 counts is a noticeable turn |
| `move` | object {forward, strafe} | The sign of each axis holds key.forward/key.back and key.right/key.left; 0 releases both |
| `pointer` | object {x, y} or array of number or null | Absolute logical window pixels from the top left, as {x,y} or [x,y]; with press:[MouseLeft] it clicks menus; null hands the pointer back to the real mouse |
| `press` | array of string | Bindings from options.txt (key.jump, key.use, key.hotbar.1, key.chat), W3C key codes (KeyW, Digit1, Space, ShiftLeft, Escape, F5) or MouseLeft/MouseRight/MouseMiddle/MouseBack/MouseForward |
| `press_frames` | integer, at least 0 | Frames a press stays down (default 1) |
| `press_ms` | integer, at least 0 | Milliseconds a press stays down instead of frames |
| `release` | array of string | Bindings from options.txt (key.jump, key.use, key.hotbar.1, key.chat), W3C key codes (KeyW, Digit1, Space, ShiftLeft, Escape, F5) or MouseLeft/MouseRight/MouseMiddle/MouseBack/MouseForward |
| `release_all` | boolean | Release every held control and the pointer first |
| `release_control` | boolean | Release everything at the end, handing input back to the real devices |
| `scroll` | object {pixels, x, y} | Same as wheel; pixels: true sends raw GameInput wheel units |
| `sneak` | boolean | Hold (true) or release (false) key.sneak |
| `sprint` | boolean | Hold (true) or release (false) key.sprint |
| `text` | string | Characters typed into the focused text field |
| `wheel` | object {unit, x, y} | Scroll; axes default 0, positive y scrolls up. unit line (default) sends whole notches, one per frame; pixel sends the values as raw GameInput wheel units (120 per notch) in one reading |

### ui_click

**Click on-screen text** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this to press a menu button, toggle, list entry or tab you can read on screen.

Moves the pointer over the label and clicks, as a player would. Works on every menu, including add-on forms, and while the window is hidden.

- First it looks for a visible button or toggle in the live UI tree whose text, or a label inside it, matches (unstable ui_tree capability, source ui_tree). Ore UI screens (world list, settings, and add-on forms when Ore UI draws them) have no tree; the oreui capability searches their elements the same way (source oreui).
- Both scroll the button's list with the wheel until at least three quarters of its height is visible, up to max_scrolls, and click its centre.
- Otherwise it reads the screen with OCR and clicks the matching line (source ocr), with a note saying why.
- A label that is exactly text wins over one that contains it, so "Villager" does not pick "Zombie Villager".
- OCR then tries a fuzzy match: one line, or neighbouring lines on a row joined, with at least 70% of the letters in order. This finds big labels OCR splits, such as Respawn.
- With OCR and scroll: true it scrolls the list under region (or the window centre) until the text appears, the list stops moving, or max_scrolls run out.
- OCR reads the game's pixel fonts, not icons or images; click those with input_send pointer at ui_tree's rectangles.
- Fails with what OCR read when the text is not found.

Returns {clicked: {text, x, y, width, height}, match (exact, contains or fuzzy), button, scrolls, source, notes}; the tree and Ore UI add control and screen, the names of the button and its screen.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` (required) | string | The label to click, matched ignoring case |
| `exact` | boolean | Only a line that is exactly text, with no contains or fuzzy match (default false) |
| `max_scrolls` | integer, at least 0 | Most wheel scrolls: to bring a UI tree button into view, or with OCR and scroll: true (default 10) |
| `region` | object {height, width, x, y} | Only click (and with OCR, look and scroll) inside this rectangle, in logical window pixels |
| `right` | boolean | Right-click instead |
| `scroll` | boolean | With OCR, scroll the list to find it (default false); the UI tree scrolls to a button it knows without it |

### ui_tree

**Read the UI tree** · reads only

Use this to see which buttons, toggles and texts a menu or the HUD shows, with their rectangles, before clicking or to check a screen's state.

Reads the live UI control tree of the top screen of each scene stack through the unstable ui_tree capability (see unstable_status). JSON UI screens have one: menus, settings, add-on forms, containers and the HUD. Read-only: the game thread reads it on its next frame.

- Ore UI screens are named by URL (ending in hbui/index.html for the world list and settings, hbui/gameplay.html for add-on forms when Ore UI draws them). The oreui capability reads them with a fixed read-only page script: focusable or clickable elements, elements labelled for tests, scrolling lists and text (source oreui, href). Without it, detail says why.
- Rectangles are [x, y, width, height] in logical window pixels, the units of input_send pointer and ui_click region.
- view controls lists buttons, toggles, text boxes, sliders, dropdowns, scroll views and free text as {kind, name, rect, text, shown}, with enabled: false, hover or checked when they apply.
- view tree nests every control under root with name, rect, components (class names such as ButtonComponent), text, checked and children.
- name is the control's JSON UI name; for Ore UI the data-testid, else data-focusable-id, else the tag, and components is the JSON UI component matching the element's role. A button's text is the labels inside it.
- shown is false when the centre lies outside its scroll view's visible part, so ui_click would scroll first.
- For Ore UI, hover means focused, and checked appears only where the page marks it (aria-checked or a checkbox).
- A read stops at 2000 controls or max_depth (Ore UI: 1500 elements or 12000 scanned) and sets truncated.
- When the game does not answer within a second, a screen is the last read, with fresh: false.
- Fails with the reason when the ui_tree capability is not active.

Returns {screens, window, notes}. Each screen has stack (the id game_status unstable.screens uses), screen (its name), nodes, truncated, read_us (game-thread read time), fresh, ui_scale (window pixels per UI unit, or per CSS pixel for Ore UI), and controls or root. notes say why an Ore UI page could not be read.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `max_depth` | integer, 0 to 64 | Levels below the root to read (default 48) |
| `stack` | integer | Only the stack with this id (game_status unstable.screens[].id) |
| `view` | `"controls"` \\| `"tree"` | controls (default): a flat list of what a player can use or read; tree: every control, nested |
| `visible_only` | boolean | Skip hidden controls and everything inside them (default true) |

### item_use

**Use item** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this to throw, shoot, eat, drink or block with the held item once. For a fight or several uses in a row, put item_use steps in one action_sequence.

mode instant clicks use once (throw, start a drink, place a boat). hold keeps use down for ms or ticks, then releases (eat, draw a bow, throw a charged weapon, block with a shield); with neither, until a call with mode release. release lets go of a held use, such as shooting the bow.

- hand offhand only states the intent for actor self, since the game picks the hand; it fails for simulated players, which only use hotbar slots.
- When actor self's use shows no event, reason says why with the Bridge pack: no_item (empty hand), cooldown (ticks left on the item's cooldown), projectile_in_flight (the item's projectile is still out near the player, such as a returning thrown weapon) or no_event.
- A simulated player's timed hold reports the event that ended the use (item_complete_use, item_release_use or item_stop_use) as evidence.completed, and the player after it as evidence.player.
- driver is input for actor self: synthetic input that aims with the Bridge pack's exact look, or /tp in a world with cheats, and checks the crosshair before clicking. It is gametest for a simulated player: SimulatedPlayer calls through the GameTest pack.
- confirmed is true only when the game showed the result: a Bridge pack event by this actor (evidence.event, with its tick), a legacy WebSocket event without the pack, or a readback (source names it).

Returns {actor, driver, confirmed, source, evidence, tick, notes, reason}. notes say why an action is unconfirmed (a blocked crosshair, an event by someone else, no way to aim); reason {class, detail} names a known cause: out_of_reach, blocked, cooldown, no_item, projectile_in_flight, no_damage, no_event or error.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | "self" (default) plays the player who ran /connect with synthetic input; the name of a GameTest simulated player calls its SimulatedPlayer methods instead |
| `hand` | `"mainhand"` \\| `"offhand"` | Default mainhand |
| `mode` | `"instant"` \\| `"hold"` \\| `"release"` | Default instant |
| `ms` | integer, at least 0 | How long mode hold keeps the item in use |
| `ticks` | integer, at least 0 | Same as ms, in game ticks of 50 ms |

### item_use_on

**Use item on block** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this to open a door or chest, press a button, till dirt, fill a bucket or place a block on a given block face.

The player aims at the centre of the face, then uses the held item on it.

- The block must be in sight and within the player's reach, which https://minecraft.wiki/w/Interaction_range gives as 5 blocks on Bedrock.
- When a simulated player's use goes unconfirmed, notes blame reach if the block is farther than the server's limit (4.5 blocks, 6 in creative).
- Confirmed by player_interact_block, item_start_use_on, item_use, or block_place on the neighbouring block.
- driver is input for actor self: synthetic input that aims with the Bridge pack's exact look, or /tp in a world with cheats, and checks the crosshair before clicking. It is gametest for a simulated player: SimulatedPlayer calls through the GameTest pack.
- confirmed is true only when the game showed the result: a Bridge pack event by this actor (evidence.event, with its tick), a legacy WebSocket event without the pack, or a readback (source names it).

Returns {actor, driver, confirmed, source, evidence, tick, notes, reason}. notes say why an action is unconfirmed (a blocked crosshair, an event by someone else, no way to aim); reason {class, detail} names a known cause: out_of_reach, blocked, cooldown, no_item, projectile_in_flight, no_damage, no_event or error.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `location` (required) | object {x, y, z} | The block to use the item on |
| `actor` | string | "self" (default) plays the player who ran /connect with synthetic input; the name of a GameTest simulated player calls its SimulatedPlayer methods instead |
| `face` | `"down"` \\| `"up"` \\| `"north"` \\| `"south"` \\| `"east"` \\| `"west"` | The face to click; without it the player aims at the block centre and uses whatever face the crosshair shows |

### attack

**Attack** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this for one melee swing at an entity or at the crosshair. For a fight until the target dies, use action_sequence with a repeated attack step.

With entity_id, actor self turns toward the entity's middle and clicks only when the crosshair shows it within reach. With the Bridge pack the turn is one re_mcp:aim write, which also reads the crosshair.

- Reach is 3 blocks in survival and 5 in creative, along the sight to the body. Beyond it the call returns at once without clicking (reason out_of_reach), unless approach is true.
- approach walks straight at the entity, re-aiming every 150 ms, until half a block inside reach (then it clicks) or approach_ms passes. evidence.approach is {walked_ms, reached, distance}.
- A walk that gets less than 0.3 blocks closer in 700 ms stops with reason blocked, evidence.approach.blocked and a note naming the block in the way (on the sight or at the player's feet).
- Confirmed by entity_hit_entity (entity_hit_block also counts without entity_id). No WebSocket event reports a melee hit, so without the Bridge pack an entity_id attack reads the target's health natively (unstable world_state capability, single player): before the swing and then once a tick for up to 2 s. A drop confirms it (source native, evidence.health {before, after, max}); a read of 0 or the entity gone confirms a kill (evidence.killed, evidence.seen health_zero or gone, where gone also covers a despawn). No drop gives reason no_damage. Without the capability it stays unconfirmed, and notes say why.
- SimulatedPlayer.attackEntity works at any distance (Microsoft Learn's SimulatedPlayer reference), so the driver refuses an entity_id beyond reach (eyes to body) and reports evidence.distance.
- When the game refuses a hit, notes say why if the pack knows (the target was just hurt, or is dead).
- driver is input for actor self: synthetic input that aims with the Bridge pack's exact look, or /tp in a world with cheats, and checks the crosshair before clicking. It is gametest for a simulated player: SimulatedPlayer calls through the GameTest pack.
- confirmed is true only when the game showed the result: a Bridge pack event by this actor (evidence.event, with its tick), a legacy WebSocket event without the pack, or a readback (source names it).

Returns {actor, driver, confirmed, source, evidence, tick, notes, reason}. notes say why an action is unconfirmed (a blocked crosshair, an event by someone else, no way to aim); reason {class, detail} names a known cause: out_of_reach, blocked, cooldown, no_item, projectile_in_flight, no_damage, no_event or error.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | "self" (default) plays the player who ran /connect with synthetic input; the name of a GameTest simulated player calls its SimulatedPlayer methods instead |
| `approach` | boolean | Actor self with entity_id: walk toward the entity when it is beyond reach, then click (default false) |
| `approach_ms` | integer, 0 to 300000 | How long approach may walk (default 5000) |
| `entity_id` | string | The entity to attack, by the id entities_list reports; without it the action applies to whatever is under the crosshair |

### entity_interact

**Interact with entity** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this to trade with, ride, feed, name or shear an entity.

Right-clicks the entity with the held item, or whatever is under the crosshair. With entity_id the player turns toward the entity and clicks only when the crosshair shows it within reach.

- A simulated player refuses an entity_id beyond reach, as for attack.

- confirmed is true only when the game showed the result: a Bridge pack event by this actor (evidence.event, with its tick), a legacy WebSocket event without the pack, or a readback (source names it).

Returns {actor, driver, confirmed, source, evidence, tick, notes, reason}. notes say why an action is unconfirmed (a blocked crosshair, an event by someone else, no way to aim); reason {class, detail} names a known cause: out_of_reach, blocked, cooldown, no_item, projectile_in_flight, no_damage, no_event or error.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | "self" (default) plays the player who ran /connect with synthetic input; the name of a GameTest simulated player calls its SimulatedPlayer methods instead |

### block_break

**Break block** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this to mine one block.

Mines until the block breaks or timeout_ms passes. Actor self holds attack, aiming at the block's centre when location is given, else on the block under the crosshair; a simulated player calls breakBlock.

- Confirmed by a block_break event at that location; without the Bridge pack by BlockBroken (self) or testforblock finding air (simulated players).
- On timeout evidence.block shows the block still there, and notes say when it may be out of reach.
- evidence.elapsed_ms is how long it took.
- driver is input for actor self: synthetic input that aims with the Bridge pack's exact look, or /tp in a world with cheats, and checks the crosshair before clicking. It is gametest for a simulated player: SimulatedPlayer calls through the GameTest pack.
- confirmed is true only when the game showed the result: a Bridge pack event by this actor (evidence.event, with its tick), a legacy WebSocket event without the pack, or a readback (source names it).

Returns {actor, driver, confirmed, source, evidence, tick, notes, reason}. notes say why an action is unconfirmed (a blocked crosshair, an event by someone else, no way to aim); reason {class, detail} names a known cause: out_of_reach, blocked, cooldown, no_item, projectile_in_flight, no_damage, no_event or error.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | "self" (default) plays the player who ran /connect with synthetic input; the name of a GameTest simulated player calls its SimulatedPlayer methods instead |
| `location` | object {x, y, z} | The block to break; required for simulated players |
| `timeout_ms` | integer, 0 to 300000 | How long to keep mining (default 10000) |

Use this to place the held block, or the one in hotbar slot, against a face of an existing block.

Works as a right click on that face: the new block goes to the neighbouring position across the face, reported as evidence.placed_at.

- Confirmed by a block_place event there, BlockPlaced without the Bridge pack, or testforblock for simulated players.
- When nothing is placed, notes say if the block may be out of reach.
- driver is input for actor self: synthetic input that aims with the Bridge pack's exact look, or /tp in a world with cheats, and checks the crosshair before clicking. It is gametest for a simulated player: SimulatedPlayer calls through the GameTest pack.
- confirmed is true only when the game showed the result: a Bridge pack event by this actor (evidence.event, with its tick), a legacy WebSocket event without the pack, or a readback (source names it).

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `face` (required) | `"down"` \\| `"up"` \\| `"north"` \\| `"south"` \\| `"east"` \\| `"west"` | The face of that block to click |
| `location` (required) | object {x, y, z} | The existing block to place against |
