### item_drop

**Drop items** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this to drop items from the selected hotbar slot.

Actor self presses key.drop once per item, or Ctrl with key.drop for the whole stack. A simulated player drops exactly quantity in one call (the pack splits the stack before dropSelectedItem).

- Actor self is confirmed by entity_spawn events of item entities near the player whose amounts add up to quantity (ItemDropped without the Bridge pack); evidence.dropped is the count seen.
- A simulated player is confirmed when the slot, read in the same tick, holds that many fewer.
- driver is input for actor self: synthetic input that aims with the Bridge pack's exact look, or /tp in a world with cheats, and checks the crosshair before clicking. It is gametest for a simulated player: SimulatedPlayer calls through the GameTest pack.
- confirmed is true only when the game showed the result: a Bridge pack event by this actor (evidence.event, with its tick), a legacy WebSocket event without the pack, or a readback (source names it).

Returns {actor, driver, confirmed, source, evidence, tick, notes, reason}. notes say why an action is unconfirmed (a blocked crosshair, an event by someone else, no way to aim); reason {class, detail} names a known cause: out_of_reach, blocked, cooldown, no_item, projectile_in_flight, no_damage, no_event or error.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | "self" (default) plays the player who ran /connect with synthetic input; the name of a GameTest simulated player calls its SimulatedPlayer methods instead |
| `quantity` | integer, 1 to 64 or any | How many items, or "stack" for the whole stack (default 1) |

### movement_set

**Move** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this to walk to a position or an entity (to), or to press movement keys (forward, strafe, jump, sneak, sprint).

With to, actor self holds forward and re-aims at the target every 150 ms until within arrival_radius blocks horizontally or timeout_ms passes. It walks straight and does not find paths. A simulated player path-finds with navigateToLocation or navigateToEntity.

- With the Bridge pack, actor self stops at the edge of water or lava ahead (evidence.liquid) unless avoid_water is false; a player already in water walks on.
- A simulated player must also be within arrival_radius plus 1 block vertically (evidence.vertical_gap is the target's height above it). It gives up at once when navigation finds no path, and after 2 s without moving.
- Manual keys stay down for duration_ms, or without it until a later call sets them to 0 or false, or the stop action.
- A simulated player moves with moveRelative and cannot sneak.
- evidence holds the start and end positions.
- driver is input for actor self: synthetic input that aims with the Bridge pack's exact look, or /tp in a world with cheats, and checks the crosshair before clicking. It is gametest for a simulated player: SimulatedPlayer calls through the GameTest pack.
- confirmed is true only when the game showed the result: a Bridge pack event by this actor (evidence.event, with its tick), a legacy WebSocket event without the pack, or a readback (source names it).

Returns {actor, driver, confirmed, source, evidence, tick, notes, reason}. notes say why an action is unconfirmed (a blocked crosshair, an event by someone else, no way to aim); reason {class, detail} names a known cause: out_of_reach, blocked, cooldown, no_item, projectile_in_flight, no_damage, no_event or error.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actor` | string | "self" (default) plays the player who ran /connect with synthetic input; the name of a GameTest simulated player calls its SimulatedPlayer methods instead |
| `arrival_radius` | number, at least 0 | Horizontal distance that counts as arrived (default 1) |
| `avoid_water` | boolean | Stop at water or lava instead of walking in (default true; actor self with the Bridge pack) |
| `duration_ms` | integer, 0 to 300000 | Hold the manual keys this long, then release them |
| `forward` | number | Positive walks forward, negative back, 0 releases both keys |
| `jump` | boolean | Hold (true) or release (false) key.jump, also while walking with to; a simulated player jumps once, and ignores it with to |
| `sneak` | boolean | Hold (true) or release (false) key.sneak; not with to, and simulated players cannot sneak |
| `sprint` | boolean | Hold (true) or release (false) key.sprint, also while walking with to; a simulated player moves at full speed, and ignores it with to |
| `strafe` | number | Positive steps right, negative left, 0 releases both keys |
| `timeout_ms` | integer, 0 to 300000 | Give up walking to the target after this long (default 20000) |
| `to` | object {x, y, z} or string | Where to walk: a position {x, y, z} or an entity id to follow |

### entity_spawn

**Spawn entity** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this to put a test mob or other entity in front of a player and get its id for attack, look or conditions. Inside a fight, prefer a spawn step in action_sequence.

Summons type with /summon at ahead, right and up blocks from the actor's feet along its facing, or at position, and finds the new entity's id. Needs cheats; works without the Bridge pack.

- With the Bridge pack the id comes from its entity_spawn event of that type near the spot (evidence.matched_by entity_spawn), else the nearest entity of the type within 2 blocks (matched_by nearest, with a note that it may be an older one).
- Without the pack the actor's place comes from querytarget, and the id is the entity of the type within 2 blocks that querytarget lists after the /summon but not before it (matched_by querytarget), looked for up to 2 s; else the nearest one there (matched_by nearest, with a note).
- With the pack it refuses a spot whose feet or head block is solid or outside the loaded chunks, naming the block; without it the spot is not checked.
- Each effect is applied with /effect on the nearest entity of the type at the spot; evidence.effects is [{id, applied, error}].
- evidence also holds id, type, location, requested_at and line_of_sight {clear, blocked_by {id, location}}: whether a ray from the actor's eyes to the entity's middle meets a block. Without the pack clear is null (unknown), with a note.
- driver is input for actor self: synthetic input that aims with the Bridge pack's exact look, or /tp in a world with cheats, and checks the crosshair before clicking. It is gametest for a simulated player: SimulatedPlayer calls through the GameTest pack.
- confirmed is true only when the game showed the result: a Bridge pack event by this actor (evidence.event, with its tick), a legacy WebSocket event without the pack, or a readback (source names it).

Returns {actor, driver, confirmed, source, evidence, tick, notes, reason}. notes say why an action is unconfirmed (a blocked crosshair, an event by someone else, no way to aim); reason {class, detail} names a known cause: out_of_reach, blocked, cooldown, no_item, projectile_in_flight, no_damage, no_event or error.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` (required) | string | Entity type id, such as minecraft:zombie or zombie |
| `actor` | string | Whose position and facing ahead, right and up count from |
| `ahead` | number | Blocks in front of the actor along its yaw (default 0) |
| `effects` | array of object {amplifier, hide, id, seconds} | Effects to give it, such as slowness 255 to keep it in place or fire_resistance against daylight |
| `name` | string | Name tag for the entity |
| `position` | object {x, y, z} | An absolute spot instead of ahead, right and up |
| `right` | number | Blocks to the actor's right; negative goes left (default 0) |
| `up` | number | Blocks above the actor's feet (default 0) |

### action_sequence

**Run action sequence** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this for any play-test with more than one action, such as a whole fight.

Runs up to 64 steps in one call (spawn mobs, switch items, aim, attack until a target dies, record), so the server reacts within a tick and a recording holds no waits between tool calls. Each step names an action and its args as the matching tool takes them.

- **Actions:** spawn takes entity_spawn's arguments and about 10 ticks. hotbar_select takes slot (0 to 8). look takes position, entity_id or block (with face). stop releases held keys and stops a simulated player, which keeps looking at a look target until its next look.
- **References:** after a spawn step with as: "A", args and conditions may write "$A" (or "$spawn:<index>") for its id; an event contains of just "$A" matches that id, so {event: {name: "entity_die", contains: "$A"}} waits for its death. An item_use step targets the entity its actor last looked at, attacked or walked to.
- **Without the Bridge pack:** the sequence reads the health of every spawned or targeted entity natively about once a tick (unstable world_state capability, single player) and adds each drop as an entity_hurt event and each death (health 0, or gone after a read showed it, which also covers a despawn) as an entity_die event, source native and the read's server tick. Event conditions, killed_by and final use them as they use the pack's. If the native read is unavailable, notes say so and kills go unseen.
- **Timing:** use at_tick (game ticks by the Bridge pack's clock, 50 ms each without it) or after_ms throughout; a step without either runs right after the one before. Steps that would start after timeout_ms are skipped.
- **Sending ahead:** with at_tick and the pack, a simulated player's step goes a second ahead and runs on its exact tick, so tick 0 is a second after the call. An actor self step that aims (attack or entity_interact with entity_id, item_use_on, block_place, block_break with location) starts up to 8 ticks early and clicks on its tick; a look starts 3 ticks early; neither before the player's previous step or the spawn step it names. started_tick is when a step ran, or when actor self's input went out.
- **Overlap:** a step finishes (event, walk, mining, hold) while later steps start. An actor self step waits only for a control an earlier one still holds: a timed item_use hold keeps key.use and the view (hotbar_select waits too), block_break keeps key.attack and the view, movement_set keeps the view and movement keys with to or approach, and the movement keys with duration_ms. notes list actions that started more than a tick late.
- **Conditions:** a step waits for wait_for (up to wait_ms), runs only if its if holds, then runs once or as repeat says; such a step is not sent ahead and holds back later steps. Conditions are checked once a tick; event conditions count events since the previous step started (since the call for the first step and stop_when).
- **Repeat:** until and stop_when are checked right before each run, so no run starts after until held. A run whose target already died or went away is skipped with reason target_dead, is not a failure, and ends the repeat.
- **Stopping:** stop_when ends the run as soon as it holds or cannot be checked, as fail_fast, max_failures, sequence_stop and a client disconnect do: steps not started are skipped, running ones are marked interrupted, and every actor that acted gets the stop action (actor self releases every held control).
- **Failures:** a failed step is reported and the rest still run. An error, an unconfirmed outcome and an unmet expect each count toward fail_fast and max_failures; expect is checked as each action settles.
- **Warm-up:** first the connected player warms up as scene_reset's warm_up does, so its held item is not frozen after a world load. "auto" does it when the run records, or plays actor self and no warm-up ran since the world loaded.
- **Recording:** record starts after the warm-up; the step clock starts with it, each step marks a chapter, and it stops once the last step settled.
- **Blocking:** a call answers when the run ends, or after blocking_limit_ms with {run_id, state: running, cursor, note} while the run goes on; fetch the result with sequence_status, which keeps the last 8 runs. background: true answers at once with {run_id, clock, planned: [{index, action, at_tick or after_ms}]}.
- **During a run:** other calls are answered between steps, and a slow one such as frame_capture delays the next step. One run goes at a time. Refused meanwhile: another action_sequence; the actor tools, look_at, hotbar_select and player_set for an actor it plays; input_send, ui_click and chat_send when it plays actor self.
- **Hits:** an attack or interaction hits when confirmed on the target. A throw or shot hits when its projectile hit the target, or the target was hurt before the next use aimed at it. An action that never went out counts only in reasons; one after the target died counts as after_death.
- **Reasons:** the action reasons plus target_dead and interrupted; projectile_in_flight also covers an empty hand right after using an item now gone from the inventory, such as a returning throw.
- **verbose: true** adds clock (tick or wall), confirmed (a count), the whole summary (first_tick, last_tick, hits_mean), warm_up and actors_stopped, and steps: each step's times, wait_for and if details, outcome (the action tool's reply) or error or skipped, expect {met, confirmed, holds}, and for a repeat its runs and what ended them.

Returns {run_id, state, timing {wall_ms, first_tick, last_tick}, summary, failed_steps, stopped, failures, error, warm_up {done, detail}, recording, notes}:
- summary.targets maps each entity id to {label, spawned_by, type, steps, hits, misses, after_death, killed_by, final, reasons}. killed_by is {step, run, tick, cause, killer, source} of the last action before its entity_die (source bridge or native), or null; final.state is dead, alive, gone or unknown.
- summary.totals counts actions, confirmed, unconfirmed, hits, misses, kills and reasons.
- failed_steps has one line per step that was skipped, failed, went unconfirmed or missed its expect: {index, action, target, ok: false, confirmed, reason, error}, where reason is an action reason, expect_unmet or skipped. A repeat gives {runs, failed, reasons} instead.
- stopped is null, or {at_ms, detail or error, by, actors_stopped} when something ended the run early. failures comes with a failure limit; recording is video_stop's report.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` (required) | array of object {action, after_ms, args, as, at_tick, expect, if, repeat, wait_for, wait_ms} | The actions to run, 1 to 64; each names an action, its args, an optional at_tick or after_ms, and optional wait_for, if and repeat |
| `actor` | string | The actor for steps and conditions that do not name one |
| `background` | boolean | Return a run_id at once and run the steps while other tool calls are served; watch with sequence_status, end with sequence_stop (default false) |
| `blocking_limit_ms` | integer, at least 0 | Longest a blocking call waits before it answers with the run_id and leaves the run going in the background (default 25000; 0 waits to the end) |
| `fail_fast` | boolean | End the sequence as stop_when does after the first action that errors, ends unconfirmed or misses its expect (default false) |
| `max_failures` | integer, at least 1 | End the sequence after this many such failures; not with fail_fast |
| `record` | boolean or object | Record the screen from the first step until the last one settled (default false) |
| `stop_when` | object {all, any, entity, event, near, not, state} | End the sequence as soon as this holds, e.g. low health; checked once a tick from the call. Exactly one of: event (an event since the step before started, by name ignoring case and text its body contains, as events_read shows them), entity (an entity of a type within radius blocks of the actor), state (a field of the Bridge pack's player state compared with a number or value; needs the pack), near (the actor within radius blocks of a position), not, all or any. |
| `timeout_ms` | integer, 0 to 300000 | Skip steps that would start later than this, and end waits and repeats then (default 60000) |
| `verbose` | boolean | Return every step's whole entry with its outcome and evidence, not only the failed_steps lines (default false) |
| `warm_up` | boolean or any | Warm up the connected player before the first step so its held item animates: "auto" (default) when the run records or no warm-up ran since the world loaded, true always, false never |

### sequence_status

**Watch a sequence run** · reads only

Use this to follow a background action_sequence, or to fetch the result of one whose blocking call answered with state running.

Reads what a run (default the latest) did since cursor since, waiting up to wait_ms for a new step result or the run's end. The last 8 runs are kept, blocking and background alike.

- Results come in the order they settled, shaped as action_sequence's steps. A repeated step's runs come one at a time, then its whole entry once the repeat ends.
- failed_steps has action_sequence's lines for the newly settled results; verbose: true puts them whole in steps.
- Once the run ended, the reply adds action_sequence's summary, timing, warm_up, recording and error where they apply, in its default or verbose shape; verbose also adds confirmed.

Returns {run_id, state (running, finished, stopped or failed), cursor (the next since), settled (results since since), failed_steps, current, failures, stopped, notes}. current is {index, run, started_tick, started_ms} of the last action started that still runs, or null.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `run_id` | string | The run_id action_sequence returned; default the latest run |
| `since` | integer, at least 0 | The cursor of the last status; default 0, every result |
| `verbose` | boolean | Return the settled results whole in steps, not only the failed_steps lines (default false) |
| `wait_ms` | integer, 0 to 30000 | How long to wait for news while the run runs (default 0) |

### sequence_stop

**Stop a background sequence** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this to end a running action_sequence early.

Ends the run as stop_when does: steps not started are skipped, running actions are marked interrupted, and every actor that acted gets the stop action, which for actor self releases every held control. Answers once the run wound down.

- A run that already ended returns its result unchanged.

Returns action_sequence's result (whole with verbose: true) with run_id and state; stopped.by is sequence_stop.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `run_id` (required) | string | The run_id action_sequence returned |
| `verbose` | boolean | Return every step's whole entry, not only the failed_steps lines (default false) |

## gametest toolset

GameTest simulated players and test runs, in the game or on a dedicated server.

### gametest_spawn

**Spawn a simulated player** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this when a test needs a second player in the world.

Spawns a GameTest simulated player. Scripts, commands and the Bridge see it by name, like a real player.

- Without location it spawns at the connected player, in that player's dimension; the two may push each other apart, so read player.location.
- The reply describes the player half a second after the spawn, so it shows items add-ons give on join.
- Fails when the name is taken.
- Needs the bedrock-mcp GameTest pack, as do gametest_list and gametest_remove: Ask the user before setting it up. Then turn on the Beta APIs experiment in the world's settings (the pack uses the beta @minecraft/server-gametest module and does not load without it), install the pack with packs_install (or export it with `cd mc/gametest && bun install && rgl run` in the bedrock-mcp repository), add it to the world, allow cheats, then run /reload all.

Returns {source, notes, player}, where player is {name, id, dimension, location, eye, yaw, pitch, headYaw, headPitch, health {current, max}, alive, gameMode, selectedSlot, selectedItem {id, amount} or null, sprinting, onGround}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (required) | string | The player's name, unique among simulated players |
| `game_mode` | `"survival"` \\| `"creative"` \\| `"adventure"` \\| `"spectator"` | The player's game mode (default survival) |
| `location` | object {x, y, z} | Where to spawn, in world coordinates |

### gametest_list

**List simulated players** · reads only

Use this to see the simulated players in the world and whether they are alive.

Lists every GameTest simulated player, whether gametest_spawn or a running test made it. Needs the bedrock-mcp GameTest pack.

- A dead one stays listed with alive false and health 0 until removed; it cannot act.

Returns {source, notes, players}, where each player is {name, id, dimension, location, eye, yaw, pitch, headYaw, headPitch, health {current, max}, alive, gameMode, selectedSlot, selectedItem {id, amount} or null, sprinting, onGround}.

No arguments.

### gametest_remove

**Remove a simulated player** · destructive

Use this to remove a simulated player you no longer need.

Disconnects a GameTest simulated player, which removes it from the world. Needs the bedrock-mcp GameTest pack.

Returns {source, notes, removed}, where removed is the name.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (required) | string | The simulated player's name (see gametest_list) |

### gametest_run

**Run GameTests** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this to run the add-on's registered GameTests in the open world.

Sends /gametest over the WebSocket. The tests come from behavior packs in the world; the game builds each structure next to the player.

- test runs `/gametest run`, tag `/gametest runset` (runsetuntilfail with until_fail), neither `runset suite:all`.
- Needs the Beta APIs experiment and cheats, not the bedrock-mcp GameTest pack.
- The reply says whether tests started, not whether they passed: the WebSocket may not carry outcomes, so read content_log_read after the tests' max ticks. gametest_server reports each result instead.

Returns {source, notes, command, message, messages}: message is the game's answer, messages the chat lines that arrived within wait_ms.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `repeat` | integer, at least 1 | Runs of a single test |
| `rotation` | integer, 0 to 3 | Quarter turns clockwise for the test structures |
| `stop_on_failure` | boolean | Stop repeating a single test at its first failure |
| `tag` | string | A test tag or class name |
| `test` | string | A registered test id, <class>:<name> |
| `until_fail` | boolean | With a tag: stop the set at the first failure |
| `wait_ms` | integer, at least 0 | How long to collect chat messages after the command (default 0) |

### gametest_server

**Run GameTests on a dedicated server** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this to run the add-on's GameTests without a game client, such as in CI.

Runs the tests on a Bedrock Dedicated Server (BDS) in a scratch folder that links the server's files, and reports every result. The world is a copy of the client world named by world, with its packs, or a fresh flat world.

- Turns on Beta APIs, turns off mob spawning, daylight and weather, runs commands, then /gametest as gametest_run does.
- Returns once every expected test has a result and output is quiet for 5 s, after idle_ms without progress, or at timeout_ms.
- Structures come from `structures/<namespace>/<name>.mcstructure` in a pack or the world; make one with `tickingarea add 0 0 0 15 0 15 gt`, `fill 0 -60 0 4 -56 4 air`, `structure save <namespace>:<name> 0 -60 0 4 -56 4 disk` (flat air starts at y -60).
- Default server: ~/.local/share/bedrock-server/current (%LOCALAPPDATA%\bedrock-server\current on Windows); download from https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/download/server/bedrock.
- BDS can trail the client: packs needing a newer engine or Script API fail to load (see errors and pack_stack).
- No tests, stalls and failures are normal replies; notes say which.

Returns {server, command, expected, passed, failed, results, timed_out, errors, pack_stack, command_replies, log, elapsed_ms, notes}: errors groups distinct ERROR lines, log is the full server output, timed_out also covers idle_ms.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `commands` | array of string | Console commands (no slash) to run before the tests; each reply is returned |
| `idle_ms` | integer, at least 1 | Stop when no test makes progress for this long (default 120000) |
| `packs` | array of string | Behavior and resource pack folders to load and apply to the world; each manifest says which kind |
| `repeat` | integer, at least 1 | Runs of a single test |
| `rotation` | integer, 0 to 3 | Quarter turns clockwise for the test structures |
| `server` | string | The BDS folder (default $BEDROCK_MCP_BDS, else the default server folder) |
| `stop_on_failure` | boolean | Stop repeating a single test at its first failure |
| `tag` | string | A test tag or class name |
| `test` | string | A registered test id, <class>:<name> |
| `timeout_ms` | integer, at least 1 | Longest the tests may run (default 900000) |
| `until_fail` | boolean | With a tag: stop the set at the first failure |
| `world` | string | A client world to copy, by name or folder id; without it the run makes a fresh flat world |

## automation toolset

The WebSocket session: commands, chat, events and waits.

### automation_connect

**Connect the WebSocket** · sets state (repeating it changes nothing more)

Use this right after world_open, before tools that need commands, events or the Bridge pack.

It connects Minecraft's WebSocket automation session to this server now, instead of when a tool first needs it. It types /connect 127.0.0.1:<port> into chat while the player is in a world and waits for the game to connect.

- Does nothing when already connected.
- WebSocket events arrive only while connected, so connect before the events you want to observe.

Returns {connected, url, connections, bridge}. bridge is whether the bedrock-mcp Bridge pack answers in this world.

No arguments.

### automation_status

**WebSocket session status** · reads only

Use this when commands or events stop arriving.

It reports the WebSocket automation session without connecting it.

- events_dropped counts events pushed out of the 512-event history; commands_lost counts commands whose connection closed before the game answered.
- When the server cannot listen it returns {listening: false, error}.

Returns {listening, url, connected, connections, subscriptions, observed_events, events_received, events_dropped, commands_lost, commands_in_flight, max_commands_in_flight, bridge}. connections counts connections accepted so far; bridge is whether the Bridge pack answered on this connection, null until checked.

No arguments.

### command_execute

**Run a command** · destructive

Use this for a one-off game command, such as /summon or /give.

It runs one command as the player over the WebSocket, without chat output. When the WebSocket is not connected it connects first by typing /connect.

- The leading / is optional; a line break fails, since it runs one command.
- Most commands need a world that allows cheats.
- `reload all` reloads every pack by reopening the world, which applies edits to behavior and resource packs and picks up newly exported development packs and new custom commands such as the Bridge's re_mcp:*. The WebSocket stops answering until the world is back, and notes say to wait_until in_world.
- Plain `reload` only reloads functions and scripts behind existing commands.

Returns {ok, status_code, status_message, body, notes}. body is the game's whole response, which some commands extend (/list adds players).

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `command` (required) | string | One command line, e.g. "time set day" or "/give @s diamond 3" |

### chat_send

**Send chat** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this to test add-on behaviour that reacts to chat.

It types a chat line as the player and confirms it by the game's PlayerMessage event. When the WebSocket is not connected it connects first by typing /connect.

- Rejects text starting with /; run commands with command_execute.
- Fails when the PlayerMessage event does not arrive within 5 s.

Returns {sent, event}. event is the PlayerMessage body.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` (required) | string | The chat line to type; must not start with / |

### events_list

**List event names** · reads only

Use this to find event names before event_subscribe or events_read.

It lists the event names events_read can return, per source, with the body fields each carries. ws holds Bedrock's legacy WebSocket events, which need event_subscribe; bridge holds script events the bedrock-mcp Bridge pack records, which need no subscription; native holds the events an action_sequence derives from native health reads when the pack is absent.

- Neither the ws nor the bridge list is exhaustive, and current Bedrock versions may send nothing for many ws names.
- PlayerMessage is always subscribed.

Returns {source, ws, bridge, native, always_subscribed, subscribed, observed: {ws, bridge}, notes}. ws, bridge and native are [{name, description}]; subscribed is the current subscriptions; observed lists the names seen in this session.

No arguments.

### event_subscribe

**Subscribe to WebSocket events** · sets state (repeating it changes nothing more)

Use this before an action whose WebSocket events you want to read.

It subscribes to legacy WebSocket events by name (see events_list). The subscriptions are sent now if the game is connected, and again on every later connection.

- Names outside the known list are subscribed too and listed in unknown, since the game may never send them.
- A name must be a letter, then letters, digits or underscores.

Returns {subscribed, added, unknown, connected, notes}. subscribed is every subscription now; added holds the names that were new.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `names` (required) | array of string | Event names such as ItemUsed or PlayerTravelled |

### event_unsubscribe

**Unsubscribe from WebSocket events** · sets state (repeating it changes nothing more)

Use this to stop WebSocket events you no longer need.

It sends unsubscribe to the game and ignores any of those events still arriving.

- Fails when names include PlayerMessage, which stays subscribed because chat_send confirms chat with it.

Returns {subscribed, removed, not_subscribed}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `names` (required) | array of string | Subscribed event names to stop; names not subscribed are listed in not_subscribed |

### events_read

**Read events** · reads only

Use this to see what an action caused: take since "now" right before it, then read from that cursor after it.

It reads one stream merging WebSocket events (source ws, see event_subscribe), Bridge pack script events (source bridge, polled with re_mcp:events) and events an action_sequence derives from native health reads without the pack (source native: entity_hurt and entity_die of its targets). Pass the returned cursor as since to continue.

- since "now" reads nothing and returns the stream's current end.
- Without since it starts at the oldest event still held: 512 WebSocket, 2048 script and 4096 native events.
- The cursor moves past events the filters skipped.
- In one read, ws events come before bridge events, and bridge before native.

Returns {source, events, cursor, dropped: {ws, bridge, native}, notes}. Events are {cursor, source, name, received_at (Unix ms; poll time for bridge), tick (bridge: script tick; native: the server tick of the read), body}. dropped counts events lost before this read; notes say why bridge events were skipped or restarted.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer, 1 to 1000 | Default 100 |
| `names` | array of string | Only these event names, ignoring case, e.g. ["PlayerMessage", "block_break"] |
| `since` | string | A cursor from an earlier events_read or from an event, or "now" for the current end of the stream |
| `sources` | array of `"ws"` \\| `"bridge"` \\| `"native"` | Only events from these sources (default all) |
| `wait_ms` | integer, 0 to 300000 | Wait up to this long for at least one event that passes the filters (default 0, no wait) |

### wait_until

**Wait for a condition** · reads only

Use this to wait for a screen, an entity, a log entry or an event instead of sleeping.

It blocks until the condition holds and fails after timeout_ms. detail.source says what answered; notes explain fallbacks.

- screen: the top screen of any live scene stack starts with name (chat_screen, pause_screen, hud_screen, ...). Needs the screens capability; polls every 50 ms.
- in_world: the scene stacks, else the WebSocket; fails at once when neither tells.
- content_log: an entry written after the call, read live with the unstable layer (level matched by number), else from the file.
- text: an OCR line containing it, ignoring case, from a capture every 250 ms; region is in logical window pixels. detail.line has its box; a timeout lists the last capture's text.
- event: the first event in events_read's stream after the call; name ignores case, contains matches the body's JSON.
- chunks_loaded and entity connect the WebSocket if needed.

Returns {satisfied, waited_ms, detail, notes}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `condition` (required) | string or object | Exactly one of: "in_world", "camera_finished", {"screen": {"name": "chat"}}, {"chunks_loaded": {"radius": 4}}, {"entity": {"matches": "minecraft:zombie", "radius": 32}}, {"content_log": {"level": "error", "contains": "text"}}, {"text": {"contains": "Resume Game", "region": {"x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 640, "height": 360}}}, {"event": {"name": "block_break", "contains": "Steve"}}; only screen.name, entity.matches and text.contains are required (radius defaults: chunks 2, entity 32) |
| `timeout_ms` | integer, at least 0 | Give up after this long (default 60000) |

### scene_save

**Save a test spot** · sets state (repeating it changes nothing more)

Use this once per test spot, so later runs can return to it with scene_reset {spot}.

It saves the player's feet position, yaw, pitch and dimension under a name, or the place given in at. Saving a name again replaces it.

- Where the player stands comes from player_get: the Bridge pack, else in single player the unstable layer's native read (no cheats needed). Commands give no feet position, so with neither, pass at.
- Spots are stored per world folder in scenes/<folder>.json in the agent directory.
- The world is the one the game wrote last (the open one) unless world names another.

Returns {source (where the spot came from: bridge, native or argument), notes, saved, spot, world: {name, folder}, spots}. spots lists every spot name saved for that world.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (required) | string | Spot name, e.g. "ice" |
| `at` | object {dimension, pitch, x, y, yaw, z} | Save this place instead of where the player stands |
| `world` | string | World name or folder id (default: the open world) |

### scene_reset

**Reset a test scene** · destructive

Use this at the start of every test run to put the player, world and inventory into a known state in one call.

It runs only the steps you give, in order: teleport, clear_entities, time, weather, difficulty, gamemode, effects, clear_inventory, give, heal, hotbar, perspective, warm_up. Then it waits settle_ms and reads the player. Commands need cheats.

- teleport (spot or teleport, not both) uses the Bridge pack's Script API, silent in chat, else /tp, then waits up to 5 s for chunks.
- clear_entities moves entities below the world instead of killing them, so nothing dies in view. Rain fades in over seconds. effects clears all effects first. heal gives instant health and saturation.
- hotbar uses the Bridge pack, else the slot key. perspective needs the unstable camera capability, else it is skipped with a note.
- warm_up swaps the hotbar slot and back and walks a block out and back to the spot, so a freshly loaded attachable animates; with player_render it checks and retries once. It reads the player through the Bridge pack, else natively in single player (taking the next slot unread and putting the player back with /tp); with neither it is skipped with a note.
- Nothing to remove, or no selector match, is ok with nothing_to_do: true; any other failed command stops with an error naming the step and the steps run.
- After a teleport the Bridge pack's raycast checks the spot: legs and head clear, not in water, 3 blocks open ahead. Without the pack, testforblock checks that the same blocks are air, so passable blocks count too, and notes say so. Problems go to spot_problems and make ok false.

Returns {ok, spot_problems, player, warm_up: {done, detail}, notes}. player is player_get's {source, dimension, location (eye instead when only commands answered), yaw, pitch, health, selectedSlot, perspective}. verbose adds world, spot, the full player and every step with its command and output.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clear_entities` | boolean or array of string | true removes every entity except players, dropped items and experience orbs included, as /kill @e[type=!player] would; a list removes only these types, e.g. ["minecraft:zombie", "minecraft:item"] |
| `clear_inventory` | boolean | Empty the inventory before give (default false) |
| `difficulty` | `"peaceful"` \\| `"easy"` \\| `"normal"` \\| `"hard"` |  |
| `effects` | array of object {amplifier, effect, seconds} | Effects to have afterwards, with particles hidden; [] only clears them |
| `gamemode` | `"survival"` \\| `"creative"` \\| `"adventure"` \\| `"spectator"` |  |
| `give` | array of object {count, item, slot} |  |
| `heal` | boolean | Fill health and hunger (default false) |
| `hotbar` | integer, 0 to 8 | Hotbar slot to select at the end |
| `perspective` | `"first_person"` \\| `"third_person_back"` \\| `"third_person_front"` |  |
| `settle_ms` | integer, 0 to 60000 | Wait this long before reading the player (default 0) |
| `spot` | string | A spot saved with scene_save in this world |
| `teleport` | object {dimension, pitch, x, y, yaw, z} | Teleport here instead of to a saved spot |
| `time` | `"day"` \\| `"noon"` \\| `"sunset"` \\| `"night"` \\| `"midnight"` \\| `"sunrise"` or integer, at least 0 | A time name or ticks |
| `verbose` | boolean | Also return the world, the spot, every step's command and output and the whole player (default false) |
| `warm_up` | boolean | Swap the hotbar slot and back and walk a block and back as the last step, so the held item's attachable animates (default true) |
| `weather` | `"clear"` \\| `"rain"` \\| `"thunder"` |  |
| `world` | string | World name or folder id whose spots to use (default: the open world) |

## media toolset

Screenshots, recordings and scripted cameras.

### frame_capture

**Capture a frame** · reads only

Use this to see the game screen, or with ocr to read its text.

Saves the game window's own buffer as a full-size PNG and returns it inline, scaled to max_width. It works while the window is hidden or covered (not minimized) and never shows other windows.

- Captured with grim -T on Hyprland, elsewhere from the newest frame the agent copies from the game.
- OCR matches the game's pixel fonts (Mojangles, Minecraft Seven/Ten/Five) from the installation, so it reads UI text exactly but not world signs, icons, textures, vector-font text (Noto, non-Latin scripts) or other overlays.
- ocr with inline: false costs far fewer tokens than an image; take an image for layout, colours or anything visual.
- Without the game fonts, ocr holds an error and the capture still succeeds.

Returns {path, size, logical_size, inline_scale, ocr?} and the image; ocr is {lines: [{text, x, y, width, height, confidence, engine}], ms} in logical pixels, top to bottom.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `inline` | boolean | Return the image (default true) |
| `max_width` | integer, at least 1 | Widest the inline image may be, in physical pixels (default 1280); the saved PNG stays full size |
| `ocr` | boolean | Also return the text lines (default false) |
| `path` | string | Where to save the PNG (default under the agent folder's screenshots/) |
| `region` | object {height, width, x, y} | Only read text inside this rectangle, in logical pixels; needs ocr |

### video_start

**Start recording** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this to record a test you will watch afterwards; for a fight in one action_sequence, pass record: true there instead.

Records the game's own frames to MP4, copied out of the game (Direct3D 12) on the GPU. It works while the window is hidden or covered, never shows other windows, and returns once the first frame arrives.

- Each video frame is the newest frame the game had presented, so stalls show as repeated frames.
- game_fps equal to fps puts every rendered frame in the video once, for frame-by-frame animation checks; leave the game uncapped to check behaviour that depends on frame rate.
- Linux encodes with VAAPI and PulseAudio; Windows with the first ffmpeg encoder that works (NVENC, AMF, Quick Sync, Media Foundation, x264, x265) and WASAPI loopback.
- On Hyprland it raises misc:render_unfocused_fps for the recording and restores it after.
- Each tool call becomes a chapter titled with the tool, short arguments and game tick, e.g. "attack -326417514479 (tick 445260)".
- pause_on_idle_ms cuts frames and audio between calls; a running call or background action_sequence never pauses it.
- Fails when a recording is already running.

Returns {recording, path, log, fps, game_fps, size, codec, pause_on_idle_ms, notes}; log is ffmpeg's log file.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audio` | boolean | Also record the default audio output into the video (default true) |
| `codec` | `"h264"` \\| `"hevc"` | Video codec (default h264) |
| `fps` | integer, 1 to 240 | Video frame rate (default 60) |
| `game_fps` | integer, 1 to 240 | Hold the game to this many frames a second while recording (default: uncapped) |
| `path` | string | Output .mp4 (default under the agent folder's recordings/) |
| `pause_on_idle_ms` | integer, at least 1 | Cut the video while no tool call has run for this many ms, until the next call (default: never cut) |

### video_stop

**Stop recording** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this right after the last recorded action returns.

Stops the recording, finishes the MP4 and reports dropped and repeated frames and the game's frame pacing.

- Every present time goes to <video>.frames.json.
- A hitch is a frame shown over twice the median frame time.
- Fails when nothing is recording or ffmpeg does not finish the file.

Returns {path, log, frame_times, elapsed_seconds, fps, size, captured_frames, missed_frames, encoder_behind_frames, skipped_frames, video_frames, repeated_frames, pacing, chapters, chapters_file, encoded_frames, duration_seconds}: pacing holds frame_ms percentiles and hitches with their time in the video; chapters_file lists the chapters. With pause_on_idle_ms it adds paused (each cut), paused_seconds and paused_frames.

No arguments.

### timeline_read

**Read the session timeline** · reads only

Use this to see how long each step of a flow took and where it sits in a recording.

Reads the tool calls this server answered, oldest first, from the JSONL file it keeps under the agent folder's timeline/.

- Pass next_since back as since to read only newer calls.

Returns {path, entries, skipped, next_since}: skipped counts calls limit left out; each entry is {seq, tool, args_summary, started_unix_ms, duration_ms, ok, error_head, tick, recording_offset_s}, with tick and recording_offset_s (where the call starts in the running video) null when unknown.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer, at least 1 | Most recent entries returned (default 50) |
| `since` | integer, at least 0 | Only calls after this seq (default: from the first) |

### video_analyze

**Analyze a recording** · reads only

Use this after a recording to find animation glitches without watching the whole video.

Finds one-frame pops, teleports and snaps: it compares each frame with the next inside region and flags changes far above the typical change of the surrounding quarter second.

- Nearby flags form one event; events are ranked by size.
- Intended changes (swings, item switches) are flagged too, so judge each from its sheet.
- Works best with game_fps equal to fps and a still camera.
- The motion graph and every sheet are also saved next to the video.

Returns {video, frames, fps, region, threshold, median_change, event_count, events, motion_graph, note}, then the motion graph (red bars flagged) and the top event sheets as images. Each event gives its frames (from 0), jump {from, to, change, typical_change, ratio}, at_seconds and sheet.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` (required) | string | The video, e.g. the path video_stop reported |
| `inline` | integer, at least 0 | Event sheets returned as images (default 3); the rest are only saved |
| `max_events` | integer, at least 1 | Events reported, largest first (default 8) |
| `region` | object {height, width, x, y} | Area to watch, in video pixels (default: the first-person held item, right of centre above the hotbar) |
| `threshold` | number, at least 1 | How many times the typical change a jump must be (default 4); lower finds more |

### camera_play

**Play a camera path** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this for a scripted camera move in a cinematic or recording.

Takes over the camera with /camera free and plays keyframes on wall-clock time, eased by the game.

- ease_in, ease_out and ease_in_out are the game's in_cubic, out_cubic and in_out_sine; step cuts at the keyframe.
- A single keyframe holds a fixed camera; a new path replaces a running one.
- Needs a world with cheats.

Returns {keyframes, duration_seconds, loop, loops_completed, elapsed_seconds, finished, error}, or {released: true}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `easing` | `"linear"` \\| `"ease_in"` \\| `"ease_out"` \\| `"ease_in_out"` \\| `"step"` | Easing for keyframes that set none (default ease_in_out) |
| `hide_hand` | boolean | Hide the HUD with /hud while scripted (default true; restored on release) |
| `keyframes` | array of object {easing, fov, pitch, position, t, yaw} | At least one keyframe, played in order of t; the path starts at the first one. Needed unless release is true |
| `loop` | boolean | Start the path over each time it ends, until release (default false) |
| `release` | boolean | Stop the path and give the camera back to the player; other arguments are ignored (default false) |

### camera_get

**Read the live camera** · reads only

Use this to check where the player's camera points and which perspective it shows.

Reads the camera through the unstable layer's camera capability (see unstable_status), without the Bridge pack or a WebSocket.

- view is the render camera; in third person front it faces the player.
- view.position is null when the camera reports the origin, which may be a camera-relative position rather than a world one; view.fov and view.aspect_ratio may be null too.
- Fails when the camera capability is not active.

Returns {perspective, perspective_age_ms, fov, fov_age_ms, view, detail}: perspective is first_person, third_person_back or third_person_front; fov is in degrees as the camera reports it, so it may include effects such as sprinting; view is {position, yaw, pitch, forward, up, fov, aspect_ratio, age_ms}, where yaw 0 faces +Z/south and positive pitch looks down; detail says why a part is missing.

No arguments.

### camera_set

**Set the camera perspective** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this to switch between first and third person before a test or recording.

Presses the key bound to key.togglePerspective (F5 by default) through the stable agent until the unstable layer's camera capability reads the wanted perspective; two presses reach any of the three.

- Fails when the camera capability is not active or has not read the perspective in the last second.
- Fails when a screen covers the HUD, or a press does not change the perspective within 1.5 s.

Returns {perspective, previous, presses, camera}, with camera as camera_get reports it.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `perspective` (required) | `"first_person"` \\| `"third_person_back"` \\| `"third_person_front"` | The perspective to switch to |

## dev toolset

Logs, packs, worlds, skins and the unstable layer.

### content_log_read

**Read the content log** · reads only

Use this after packs load or reload, and after each test step, to catch pack and script errors.

Reads this game session's content log entries (pack and script errors and warnings) after since, waiting up to wait_ms for one. Pass the reply's cursor back as since to continue.

- auto reads live entries from the unstable layer's content_log capability when active, else the log file; a failed live read falls back to the file with a note.
- Cursors are live@<seq> or <file>@<offset>. A file cursor continues the file; a live cursor fails with source file and restarts the file when auto falls back.
- File entries are {time, area, level, message} with level names; live entries are {seq, area, level, area_name, level_name, message} with numeric area and level.
- Use summary first when a pack floods the log: hundreds of errors usually come from a few causes.

Returns {entries, cursor, source, notes}, plus dropped (entries the live buffer lost). summary replaces entries with total and groups [{level, area, pattern, count, values, example}], most frequent first: pattern is the first line with variable parts as *, values the distinct count and up to 5 samples per *.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `levels` | array of string | Only entries at these levels, ignoring case: names (verbose, info, warning, error) or, for live entries, numbers too (default every level) |
| `since` | string | Cursor from a previous call |
| `source` | `"auto"` \\| `"live"` \\| `"file"` | Where entries come from: the unstable layer (live), the log file, or live when it can (auto, the default) |
| `summary` | boolean | Group entries by cause instead of listing them (default false) |
| `wait_ms` | integer, at least 0 | Wait up to this long for at least one matching entry (default 0, no wait) |

### log_levels_set

**Set log levels** · sets state (repeating it changes nothing more)

Use this when you need more or less detail from an area in the game's debug log (in its logs folder).

Sets the debug log filter in options.txt for the next launch. Minecraft may rewrite options.txt when it exits, so this fails while the game runs.

- Levels are verbose, info, warn and error; area all means every area.
- Bedrock keeps one set of areas and one of priorities, so every named area logs from the most verbose level named.

Returns {spec, effective, applies_on_next_launch}; effective is what log_levels_get would report.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spec` (required) | string | Comma-separated area=level directives, e.g. all=warn,ui=error |

### log_levels_get

**Get log levels** · reads only

Use this to see which debug log areas and levels are on.

Reads the debug log filter from options.txt, whether or not the game runs.

Returns {areas, priorities, spec}.

No arguments.

### packs_global

**Global resource packs** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this to switch global resource packs.

Reports the installed resource packs and the active global ones, top priority first. activate and deactivate stage changes in this session; apply writes global_resource_packs.json.

- activate puts available[index] at the top of active; deactivate removes active[index].
- The game reads the file at startup, so applying while it runs reports restart_required: true.

Returns {available, active, pending, restart_required}: pending says staged changes are not applied yet; restart_required is null unless this call applied.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `"apply"` or object {activate} or object {deactivate} | apply, {activate: {index}} or {deactivate: {index}}; indices follow the last reported available or active list |

### worlds_list

**List worlds** · reads only

Use this to find a world's name, folder id and packs before world_open or world_packs_set.

Lists the local worlds from their files, whether or not the game runs. Each pack is its name, or its uuid when not installed.

- verbose or world gives each pack as {pack_id, version, name, location, folder}, with null name, location and folder when not installed.
- Worlds can share a name; the folder id tells them apart.

Returns {worlds: [{name, folder, last_played, behavior_packs, resource_packs}]}; last_played is UTC text or null.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verbose` | boolean | Every pack in full: uuid, version, name, location and folder (default false) |
| `world` | string | Only this world, in full: a folder id, or a name (every world of that name) |

### world_packs_set

**Set a world's packs** · destructive

Use this to add your add-on, the Bridge pack or the GameTest pack to a closed world, when the user asked for it.

Replaces the behavior or resource pack list (or both) a local world applies. The game reads them when it next opens the world. Never add the Bridge or GameTest pack to a world on your own: ask the user first.

- Each pack is looked up in the world's packs, then development_*_packs, then *_packs; the version comes from its manifest.
- Refused while the game is in a world, because the game may rewrite the lists when it closes the world (call world_leave first); when that cannot be told, it writes and notes the risk.
- Fails when neither list is given or a pack is not found.
- Does not turn on experiments such as Beta APIs.

Returns the world as worlds_list with world shows it, plus note and notes.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `world` (required) | string | World name or folder id |
| `behavior` | array of string | The world's full behavior pack list, top priority first: each a pack uuid, folder name or manifest name |
| `resource` | array of string | The world's full resource pack list, top priority first: each a pack uuid, folder name or manifest name |

### packs_install

**Install the bedrock-mcp packs** · sets state (repeating it changes nothing more)

Use this when the user agreed to install the Bridge or GameTest pack, or with check: true to see whether they are missing or older than this server.

Writes the Bridge and GameTest behavior packs built into this server into development_behavior_packs, so their commands match it.

- A new pack shows up after a restart, an updated one after /reload all; notes say which while the game runs.
- Never install without check: true on your own: suggest it to the user when a tool says it needs the pack, and wait for a yes.
- Then add them with world_packs_set; the GameTest pack also needs the Beta APIs experiment.
- Fails, naming the export commands, when this build embeds no packs.

Returns {packs: [{uuid, version, folder, path, status, before, written}], notes}: status is missing, outdated, current, or updated with before; written says this call wrote it.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check` | boolean | Only compare the installed copies (default false) |

### skin_install

**Install a skin pack** · sets state (repeating it changes nothing more)

Use this to test a skin pack.

Installs a skin pack folder, .mcpack or .zip (manifest.json and skins.json) into development_skin_packs; the Dressing Room lists it after a restart.

- Single PNG skins are refused: Bedrock imports them only through the Dressing Room's file picker.

Returns {installed, name, restart_required, note}; installed is the new folder.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` (required) | string | A skin pack folder, .mcpack or .zip on this machine |

### unstable_status

**Unstable layer status** · acts (repeating it acts again)

Use this when a tool notes that an unstable capability is missing, failed or pending.

Reports the optional unstable layer (bedrock_unstable.dll, which reads game internals), loading it once the stable agent is attached.

- It loads on any build; BEDROCK_MCP_UNSTABLE=0 turns it off.
- A failed load is retried only after the game restarts.
- Each capability checks itself and, when failed or unavailable, says why without affecting the others.
- Stable tools never fail because of it; they fall back with a note.

Returns {setting, enabled, pid, load, status, note}: load is {state: not_loaded, loaded or failed, detail}; status is the DLL's build and capabilities, or null.

No arguments.

### player_render_get

**Read the player's animation state** · reads only

Use this to check which animations and animation controllers play on the player.

Reads the local player's client animation components, with their controllers, animations and attachables, through the unstable layer's player_render capability. The game reads each one on its own thread the next time it evaluates it.

- In first person the client component's root controller is in first_person and draws the arms and held item; client_hud is the model menus show.
- A frozen attachable is a child with no players, controllers in the wrong state for the held item, or frames_behind and applied.age_ms growing between calls.
- Without a WebSocket connection the layer knows the player only once a menu showed its model or first person ran; detail says so.
- Fails when the capability is not active.

Returns {frame, components, visits_by_group, detail}. Each component has group, owner (AnimationComponentID), last_update_frame, frames_behind (lag behind frame), applied (last pose application, or null), read_age_ms, read_us, players and children; each player has kind, name, state, state_index (-1: none yet), last_state_index, state_time (s) and animations. visits_by_group counts evaluations per group index since load.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wait_ms` | integer, 0 to 2000 | Wait up to this long for each component to be evaluated again (default 250) |

### perf_get

**Read frame timings** · reads only

Use this to measure frame times while your add-on runs.

Summarises the game's recent frame and update timings (last 1024 samples, or window_ms) through the unstable layer's perf capability.

- frame_ms: time between frame starts (MinecraftGame::update); update_ms: that call's wall time; game_update_ms: getGameUpdateDurationInSeconds; scene_frame_ms: time between updates of one UI scene stack.
- A large newest_age_ms means the game is stalled or not drawing.
- Fails when the capability is not active.

Returns {window_ms, long_frame_ms, newest_age_ms, frame_ms, update_ms, game_update_ms, scene_frame_ms, recent}: each series is {count, mean, min, p50, p90, p95, p99, max} in ms (nearest rank) or null, frame_ms and scene_frame_ms add fps and long; recent holds each series' newest values.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `long_frame_ms` | number, at least 0 | Frames longer than this count as long (default 50) |
| `recent` | integer, 0 to 256 | Newest values to list per series (default 16) |
| `window_ms` | number, at least 0 | Only samples from the last window_ms (default every kept sample) |

## docs toolset

Pack validation, pack fixes, Bedrock JSON schemas and Molang; needs no game.

### pack_validate

**Validate a pack** · reads only, may reach other machines

Use this to find a pack's errors without starting the game, before testing it or after you edit it.

Checks a behavior or resource pack, or a folder of packs, with Minecraft Creator Tools. The pack is not changed.

- Runs mct from BEDROCK_MCP_MCT or PATH, else npx @minecraft/creator-tools@0.21.0; needs Node.js 22 or newer.
- suite main runs the common checks, addon the packaging checks, all every check.
- exit_code is 0 for no problems, 3 errors, 4 failed checks, 5 an internal MCT error; findings are kept for each.
- Some checks download vanilla data.

Returns {source: "mct", ok, exit_code, findings: [{severity, rule, file, message, data?}], counts, projects, mct_version, notes}: severity is error, warning, recommendation or internal_error, rule an id such as CPACKICON, file relative to the pack.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` (required) | string | A pack or project folder, or a .mcpack, .mcaddon, .mcworld or .zip file |
| `exclude` | array of string | Rule ids to skip, as in a finding's rule |
| `suite` | `"main"` \\| `"addon"` \\| `"all"` | Which checks to run (default main) |
| `warn_only` | boolean | Make MCT exit 0 even with errors; findings are still reported (default false) |

### pack_info

**Pack information** · reads only, may reach other machines

Use this to see what a pack or project contains before you work on it.

Describes a pack or project with Minecraft Creator Tools (`mct info`): its name, behavior and resource pack folders, the items it contains by type and path, and error counts.

- Finds mct as pack_validate does and needs Node.js 22 or newer.

Returns MCT's fields plus source "mct", mct_version and notes.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` (required) | string | A pack or project folder, or a .mcpack, .mcaddon, .mcworld or .zip file |

### pack_fix_versions

**Update pack versions** · sets state (repeating it changes nothing more), may reach other machines

Use this when validation reports outdated min_engine_version or format_version values.

Raises a pack folder to the newest versions Minecraft Creator Tools knows. By default it runs the fix on a temporary copy and changes nothing; dry_run: false edits the files in path.

- MCT rewrites each file it changes in its own JSON layout.
- Needs Node.js 22 or newer.

Returns {source: "mct", dry_run, fix, updated_count, changed: [{file, changes: [{field, before, after}]}], mct_version, notes}.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fix` (required) | `"min_engine_version"` \\| `"format_versions"` | min_engine_version sets header.min_engine_version in manifests; format_versions sets format_version in definition files |
| `path` (required) | string | A pack or project folder |
| `dry_run` | boolean | Fix a temporary copy and only report the changes (default true) |

### schema_list

**List Bedrock schemas** · reads only, may reach other machines

Use this to find which schema describes a pack file type or component before you write one.

Lists the pack file types that rockide/schemas 0.1.4 describes; with query, only matching documents plus matching components. The release's source archive is downloaded once with curl into the cache.

- Components are the namespaced keys (minecraft:health) each type's newest format_version schema reaches.
- Fails when curl is missing or the download fails and nothing is cached; the error names the URL.

Returns {source: "rockide", version, documents: [{id, title, pack, file_match, format_versions, component_count, description}], components?: [{kind, component}], truncated?, notes}: file_match globs are relative to the pack folder, format_versions are the ones with their own schema, oldest first.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string | Text to find, ignoring case, in document ids, titles, descriptions and component names, e.g. health (default: every document) |

### schema_get

**Get a Bedrock schema** · reads only, may reach other machines

Use this to read the exact fields a pack file or component takes.

Reads one JSON schema from the release schema_list uses: give id, or kind with an optional component. A file type's schema is the one for its newest format_version unless format_version picks another.

- A component is the first property of that name the type's schema reaches through its $refs; when it is a $ref, the schema it points to.
- Fails when nothing matches, kind is ambiguous or format_version is unknown; the error says where to look.

Returns {source: "rockide", version, id, schema, refs, kind?, component?, format_version?, notes}: id and refs are schema ids (a file, with #/pointer for a part of one) to pass back as id.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `component` | string | A component of kind, with or without the minecraft: prefix (minecraft:health or health) |
| `format_version` | string | The file's format_version, e.g. 1.21.0, with kind or a document id (default: the newest in format_versions) |
| `id` | string | A document id from schema_list (bp/entities) or a schema id from refs (bedrock/server/entity/legacy/components/health); not with kind |
| `kind` | string | A document id, the same without its pack (entities, attachables), its title or its schema folder (server/entity); not with id |

### molang_eval

**Evaluate Molang** · reads only, may reach other machines

Use this to check a Molang expression's numbers without the game, such as an animation curve.

Evaluates a Molang expression with molangjs 1.7.1, run by Node.js or Bun and fetched once into the cache.

- It does not validate: unknown names become 0 and bad syntax gives a wrong number. The game reports real Molang errors in the content log when it loads the pack.
- Trigonometry takes degrees like the game unless use_radians.

Returns {source: "molangjs", value or values: [{input, value}], unsupplied, molangjs_version, runtime, notes}: unsupplied lists the names the expression read that were neither supplied nor implemented by molangjs, so evaluated as 0.

| Argument | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `expression` (required) | string | The Molang expression to evaluate |
| `queries` | object | Values for names the expression reads, e.g. {"query.anim_time": 0.5, "v.x": "math.sin(45)"}: numbers or Molang sub-expressions |
| `sweep` | object {from, name, steps, to} | Evaluate once per value of name: steps evenly spaced values between from and to, both included |
| `use_radians` | boolean | Trigonometry takes radians instead of degrees (default false) |

## Prompts

Ready flows that name the exact tools and arguments for common jobs. A client lists them with `prompts/list` and fills one in with `prompts/get`.

### playtest_item

**Play-test an item**

Test an item in a world against a spawned entity in one recorded action_sequence, then report what happened from its summary.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `item` (required) | The item id to test, e.g. example:ruby_sword |
| `world` (required) | The world's name as the world list shows it, or its folder id (see worlds_list) |
| `target` | The entity type to fight (default minecraft:zombie) |
| `distance` | How many blocks ahead of the player the target spawns (default 3) |
| `spot` | The scene_save spot the fight starts from; the flow saves it once when the world has none by that name (default arena) |

### record_combat

**Record a combat clip**

Record a clean clip of an item fighting a spawned entity: the whole setup happens before the recording starts, and the fight runs in one action_sequence.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `item` (required) | The item id to test, e.g. example:ruby_sword |
| `world` (required) | The world's name as the world list shows it, or its folder id (see worlds_list) |
| `target` | The entity type to fight (default minecraft:zombie) |
| `distance` | How many blocks ahead of the player the target spawns (default 3) |
| `spot` | The scene_save spot the fight starts from; the flow saves it once when the world has none by that name (default arena) |

### debug_pack_errors

**Debug pack errors**

Find out why a pack misbehaves: read the content log, validate the pack, check that the world applies it, and reload.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `pack` (required) | The behavior or resource pack folder on this machine |
| `world` (required) | The world's name as the world list shows it, or its folder id (see worlds_list) |

### test_ui_flow

**Test a UI flow**

Click through menus or add-on forms by their labels, checking each screen with the UI tree.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `clicks` (required) | The labels to click in order, separated by >, e.g. Settings > Video |
| `expect` | What the last screen must show (default: the screen the last click opens) |
